title: Give File Bytes the Right Home
description: A first-version file-sharing service stores large files plus ownership and access permissions. Search is not required yet. Which baseline fits?

options.text: Keep bytes and permissions only in an expiring cache.
options.explanation: An expiring cache is not the durable source of truth for either the file or its access rules.

options.text: Use a search index as the only file and permission store.
options.explanation: Search is a derived retrieval mechanism, not the authoritative store needed here; it also adds an unrequested feature.

options.text: Put bytes in object storage and metadata and permissions in a database.
options.explanation: The stores have different jobs: object storage moves large payloads; the database owns metadata and authorization state.

options.text: Introduce global sharding before tracing an upload.
options.explanation: No measured capacity need justifies sharding yet. First make an authorized upload and download work end to end.
